# ADR-0003: Generated files must not move between the dod run, the review and the commit

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Date:** 2026-10-11
- **Deciders:** volodya4u (user), Claude

## Context

`pr-evidence` binds two records to the head commit by fingerprint (`scripts/dod-fingerprint.mjs`): the dod run to the
**code** fingerprint (every file except `.agent-log/`, `docs/`, `*.md` and `target/dod/`) and the reviewer's verdict to the
**tree** fingerprint (every file except the agent log). A file that changes after dod ran, or after the review, makes the
matching gate read "files changed after …" and the run or the review has to be repeated.

Two kinds of generated file did that:

- `trace/acceptance-contracts.json` was tracked, counted as code, and written by `scripts/check-acceptance-methods.mjs`
  (both modes) whenever someone ran it. Nothing in the pre-commit hook or CI refreshes or compares it (CI runs
  `--mode=existence`). In slice H3 it was run by hand after dod and the first review, so both gates went red on the head
  commit and were repeated. ADR-0002 already listed untracking it as a possible follow-up, and slice H6's task list (`openspec/changes/harden-frontend-specs/tasks.md` (since archived as `openspec/changes/archive/2026-10-12-harden-frontend-specs/`)) already carried a
  workaround: keep the file an existence-mode record and do not leave artifact-mode output in the tree.
- `trace/trace.json` and `trace/trajectory.json` are rewritten by the pre-commit hook at commit time and also count as
  code, and `check-traceability.mjs --check-fresh` compares only the Markdown report, not the JSON. If they are stale when
  dod runs, the hook changes them in the commit and the verified tree is not the committed one. Slices H3 and H5 avoided
  this only because the reports were regenerated by hand before dod.

**Correction.** The H3 notes (and the body of pull request #75) said the pre-commit hook rewrote
`trace/acceptance-contracts.json`. It did not: the hook runs only the traceability and trajectory generators. The manual run
of `check-acceptance-methods.mjs` did.

## Decision

- **Untrack `trace/acceptance-contracts.json` and ignore it.** It is the output of a manual script that nothing validates;
  `scripts/ledger-report.mjs` already copes with it being absent.
- **`scripts/dod.mjs` regenerates the hook-owned reports first**, using the same list the hook runs (`GENERATED` in
  `scripts/hooks-pre-commit.mjs`), before it takes the code fingerprint. It is a "Generated reports" row in the evidence
  table and fails the run if a generator fails, as the hook would refuse the commit. A green dod run therefore verifies
  the files the commit will store, and the reviewer, who runs after dod, reads the same files.
- The fingerprints themselves are unchanged.

## Alternatives considered

| Option | Pros | Cons |
|---|---|---|
| Untrack the manual file and regenerate in dod (chosen) | The verified, reviewed and committed trees agree; no weaker review | dod rewrites two generated files in the working tree, so a change to a requirement or a test annotation shows up as a modified report after dod |
| Exclude the generated files from both fingerprints | Nothing to regenerate | A hand-edited generated file would no longer invalidate the review; only `--check-fresh` on the Markdown report would catch it, and not the JSON |
| `--check-fresh` in dod instead of regenerating | Non-mutating, like CI | Compares only the Markdown report, so a stale `trace/*.json` would still slip through |
| Rely on remembering to regenerate | No change | Already cost a repeated dod run and review in H3 |

## Consequences

- The `Generated reports` row appears first in every dod table. `pr-evidence` reads check names from the record, so older
  records still read.
- Running `check-acceptance-methods.mjs` by hand is now safe at any point: its output is ignored by git.
- `gate-status.mjs` no longer leaves a modified tracked file behind from the acceptance check; the other generated files it
  touches (`docs/qa/`, `trace/*.json`, `trace/ledger.jsonl`) are still the trap ADR-0002 describes.
- Not decided here (*update 2026-10-12: the retro-tagging was done in its own slice, and the archiving in ADR-0004*): retro-tagging the old tests so that `check-acceptance-methods.mjs --mode=artifact` passes, and archiving
  the finished `harden-*` OpenSpec changes. The first is planned as its own slice; the second would swap "not archived"
  warnings for missing `design.md` and `review-findings.json` warnings and is left alone.
